integration_issues.issue: Spec claims ExpressBookingConfirmation should auto-redirect parcel+success to /track after 1.2s, but no such useEffect/setTimeout is implemented in /app/frontend/src/pages/express/ExpressWizard.jsx (only a manual 'Track order' button navigates to /track). Users must click the button to reach the live-tracking page after confirmation. Not blocking — the button and live-tracking page both work — but spec-vs-code drift.

action_items: Optional: add the auto-redirect setTimeout(() => navigate(`/express/booking/${booking.id}/track`), 1200) inside ExpressBookingConfirmation useEffect when booking.booking_type==='parcel' && success, to match the spec statement in the review request.
critical_code_review_comments: dispatch.py `assign_driver_to_booking` uses the correct atomic pattern — updating with filter {is_available: true} and checking modified_count, which prevents race conditions when two bookings hit the same driver simultaneously. Good.
tracking.py `ConnectionManager.broadcast` prunes dead sockets under a lock — safe against slow/dead clients crashing the simulator. Good.

tracking.py `run_demo_simulation` transitions driver_assigned → arriving with NO asyncio.sleep in between, so `driver_assigned` state is only observable via WebSocket subscribers (not REST polling). This is why REST-polling tests can miss it. The persisted timeline still contains driver_assigned so history is intact. Consider a brief `await asyncio.sleep(2)` between driver_assigned and arriving to make the assignment feel more real to customers (currently the UI stepper visibly flashes through driver_assigned).

routes.py `create_parcel_booking` schedules run_demo_simulation via BackgroundTasks — correct. Note: BackgroundTasks fire AFTER the HTTP response, and run_demo_simulation already sleeps 1s at the top before touching the DB — well-behaved.

routes.py `driver_advance_status` is missing driver-auth (JWT). Acceptable for Phase 2 scaffolding (a comment says Phase 5), but do not deploy to production without adding it — it can currently be called by anyone who knows a booking id.
ExpressLiveTracking.jsx WebSocket has proper reconnect (3s timer) + cleanup on unmount + guards against message parsing errors. Good implementation.

The spec-claimed auto-redirect (parcel+success→/track after 1.2s) is missing from ExpressWizard.jsx `ExpressBookingConfirmation`. Only a manual 'Track order' button navigates. Users still get there, just one extra click.
seed.py `seed_express_drivers` is phone-idempotent — re-runs update phase-2 fields without duplicating docs. Uses golden-angle (137.5°) to distribute drivers around country centers. Good pattern.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Phase 2 backend + frontend are working end-to-end. Test file `/app/backend/tests/test_express_phase2.py` includes a slow (~2 min) TestFullDemoLifecycle test — either exclude via `-k 'not FullDemoLifecycle'` for fast smoke or run standalone. WebSocket connectivity uses wss:// on the preview URL. rca_of_the_issue: No production bugs found. One spec-vs-code drift: ExpressBookingConfirmation does not auto-redirect to /track (spec said 1.2s auto-redirect, code only has a manual button). RCA: the review request describes intended behaviour that was not implemented, or was removed. Impact: minor UX — customer manually clicks 'Track order'. Mitigation: add `useEffect(() => { if (success && booking.booking_type==='parcel') { const t=setTimeout(()=>navigate(`/express/booking/${booking.id}/track`), 1200); return ()=>clearTimeout(t); } }, [booking, success]);`
